question: What is the main goal of clinical governance in healthcare?

options.A: Eliminating the need for written medical records in the ward
options.B: Reducing the monthly salaries of senior nursing staff members
options.C: Continuously improving care quality and safeguarding high standards
options.D: Increasing the number of private patient rooms in the hospital

explanation: Clinical governance provides the structural framework for health facilities to maintain and improve the overall quality of services delivered to patients. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T3#BMP217_U2_T3_h1)

question: Which option is NOT a core pillar of clinical governance in midwifery practice?

options.A: Active involvement of patients and families
options.B: Routine clinical audits of maternity charts
options.C: Strict risk management to protect mothers
options.D: Mandatory private financial investment by staff

explanation: Clinical governance focuses on patient safety, risk reduction, audits, and education, rather than requiring personal financial contributions from healthcare workers. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T3#BMP217_U2_T3_h1)

question: What is the final step in completing a full clinical audit cycle?

options.A: Writing a formal request for government funding
options.B: Destroying all old patient delivery case files
options.C: Firing staff members who failed to follow the protocol
options.D: Conducting a re-audit to measure if care has improved

explanation: After implementing changes, a re-audit is essential to close the loop and verify whether the new interventions successfully improved clinical practice. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T3#BMP217_U2_T3_h2)

question: A maternity ward notices high rates of postpartum hemorrhage and wants to start an audit. What should be their very first step?

options.A: Immediately purchase new brands of intravenous fluids
options.B: Stop all normal vaginal deliveries in the primary health center
options.C: Punish all midwives who recorded high blood loss last month
options.D: Define the best practice standard for managing the third stage of labor

explanation: Before collecting data or making changes, an audit must begin by establishing clear, evidence-based standards of care against which practice will be measured. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T3#BMP217_U2_T3_h2)

question: What primary source should form the foundation of a newly written midwifery clinical protocol?

options.A: Personal opinions of the most senior nurse on duty
options.B: Unverified stories shared on social media platforms
options.C: Old practice manuals from several decades ago
options.D: Reliable research evidence and national health guidelines

explanation: Evidence-based protocols must draw from established research and authorized clinical guidelines to ensure patient safety and care quality. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T3#BMP217_U2_T3_h3)

question: Why is it important for a midwifery protocol to fit the local resource setting?

options.A: To ensure the steps are practical and realistic for the available equipment
options.B: To make sure foreign staff can easily ignore local health needs
options.C: To reduce the total number of pregnant women attending antenatal care
options.D: To bypass the need for any form of clinical audit or monitoring

explanation: Protocols must account for available drugs, staff strength, and equipment in the facility so that midwives can actually follow them in daily practice. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T3#BMP217_U2_T3_h3)

question: Which type of clinical indicator measures the final health result of the mother or baby?
explanation: Outcome indicators look at the ultimate result of care, such as recovery rates, complications, or survival statistics. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T3#BMP217_U2_T3_h4)

question: Checking whether every woman in labor had her fetal heart rate monitored every thirty minutes is an example of which indicator type?
explanation: Monitoring actions and clinical procedures performed during care delivery fall under process indicators. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T3#BMP217_U2_T3_h4)

question: What does a retrospective chart review involve in a clinical audit?

options.A: Interviewing pregnant women currently sitting in the antenatal waiting hall
options.B: Observing a midwife conduct a live vaginal delivery in the labor room
options.C: Examining already completed patient case files and registers from the past
options.D: Checking the expiry dates of drugs inside the pharmacy storeroom

explanation: Retrospective reviews look backward by analyzing past medical records and delivery registers to assess previous clinical care. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T3#BMP217_U2_T3_h5)

question: Why can poor documentation in delivery registers negatively affect the results of a clinical audit?

options.A: Unrecorded actions are treated as if the care was never provided
options.B: It automatically increases the financial budget of the maternity unit
options.C: It forces the hospital to buy brand new delivery couches
options.D: It prevents patients from ever returning to the antenatal clinic

explanation: Auditors rely entirely on written records; if a procedure is omitted from the notes, it cannot be verified and counts against compliance rates. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T3#BMP217_U2_T3_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of comparing audit data against a benchmark standard?

options.A: To calculate the monthly tax deductions for hospital employees
options.B: To measure the gap between current practice and expected quality
options.C: To test the physical strength of the delivery room furniture
options.D: To determine how many patients were admitted with malaria

explanation: Comparing findings against benchmarks shows precisely where clinical care meets expectations and where performance falls short. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T3#BMP217_U2_T3_h6)

question: Why is it important to investigate the root cause behind a poor audit finding?

options.A: To ensure the corrective intervention targets the real problem
options.B: To delay implementing any changes on the maternity ward
options.C: To find a junior staff member to blame for the failure
options.D: To increase the paperwork required for the next audit cycle

explanation: Understanding why a standard was missed prevents wasting time on solutions that do not address the true underlying barrier. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T3#BMP217_U2_T3_h6)

question: What does the phrase 'closing the audit loop' mean in quality improvement?

options.A: Shutting down the maternity ward for thorough cleaning
options.B: Stopping all clinical meetings until the end of the year
options.C: Conducting a re-audit to check if changes successfully improved care
options.D: Destroying old audit data so no one else can read it

explanation: The loop is closed when you implement changes and return to measure practice again, confirming whether quality actually improved. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T3#BMP217_U2_T3_h7)

question: A maternity unit implemented staff training after an audit showed poor partograph use. What should they do next in the audit process?

options.A: Punish any midwife who still struggles to plot the fetal heart rate
options.B: Wait a few months and perform a re-audit to assess partograph compliance
options.C: Transfer all the trained midwives to the pediatric outpatient department
options.D: Assume the problem is solved forever and never check records again

explanation: Following up with a re-audit after an intervention is the only way to verify if the training actually changed daily clinical habits. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T3#BMP217_U2_T3_h7)
